demographics.trauma_type: Accidentally caused serious injury to another

Maladaptive Strategies.value: Seeing other people that were involved in the event or that look similar

Memory.value: I can talk about what happened very easily.
Remembering the event brings back the same terror I felt at the time
My memories of the frightening event are like a film that plays over and over.

Negative Appraisals.value: My beliefs about how the world works have been completely destroyed
I am not sure my life is worth living anymore
I will never be able to feel normal emotions again

issues.item: Memory: Verbal Access: I can talk about what happened very easily.
issues.explanation: Within the Memory node, 'I can talk about what happened very easily' sits in tension with 'Remembering the event brings back the same terror I felt at the time' and 'My memories ... are like a film that plays over and over.' Severe intrusive, highly affect-laden replay is hard to reconcile with very easy verbal access; this combination is clinically possible but sufficiently contradictory to question coherence.

For trauma of accidentally causing serious injury to another, 'Sirens' can be plausible if emergency response was salient, but paired with the rest of the profile there is little supporting content about emergency-response cues or authority/rescue contexts. The trigger pattern is otherwise centered on victims/unpredictability, so this item feels weakly anchored and may not fit the same trigger network.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Enclosed Spaces: Enclosed or confined spaces
issues.explanation: 'Avoid enclosed spaces' is poorly matched to the stated trauma type and the rest of the profile. Nothing in the triggers, memory, or appraisals suggests confinement, entrapment, or claustrophobic aspects of the event, making this strategy look like it targets a symptom cluster not otherwise represented in the formulation.

issues.item: Memory: Verbal Access: I can talk about what happened very easily.
issues.explanation: The memory profile is internally inconsistent: 'I can talk about what happened very easily' sits uneasily with 'remembering the event brings back the same terror' and 'memories are like a film that plays over and over.' Although trauma survivors can sometimes recount events despite distress, this specific item implies unusually unproblematic verbal access that conflicts with the otherwise highly intrusive, emotionally overwhelming memory pattern.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Enclosed Spaces: Enclosed or confined spaces
issues.explanation: 'Avoid enclosed spaces' is not clinically well aligned with the stated trauma type of accidentally causing serious injury to another, nor with the rest of the trigger set (victim reminders, unpredictability, sirens). It suggests a confinement-related danger theme that is otherwise absent from the profile, making this item hard to explain within the same formulation.

issues.item: Memory: Verbal Access: I can talk about what happened very easily.
issues.explanation: The memory profile is internally inconsistent: saying he can talk about what happened very easily conflicts with simultaneously reporting highly intrusive, terror-laden replaying memories. In a severe PTSD presentation, these can sometimes coexist, but 'very easily' is too strong and suggests unusually low avoidance/disorganization relative to the rest of the node.

For trauma of accidentally causing serious injury to another, sirens are not impossible triggers, but paired with the rest of the profile they imply an emergency-response cueing pattern that is not otherwise reflected in the appraisals or strategies. The main trauma-linked cues are victim reminders and unpredictability; sirens stand out as weakly integrated rather than forming a coherent trigger cluster.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Enclosed Spaces: Enclosed or confined spaces
issues.explanation: Avoiding enclosed spaces is hard to explain from the stated trauma and is not supported by the other nodes. Nothing in the triggers, memory, or appraisals suggests confinement, entrapment, or panic-in-closed-spaces phenomena. This strategy appears to target a different fear domain than the rest of the profile.
